diagnosis: Lynch syndrome–associated upper tract urothelial carcinoma
legend: Although features such as prominence of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (as apparent by H&E stain here) have been described for Lynch syndrome–associated urothelial carcinoma, such features are insufficiently specific to recognize cases prospectively. Instead, increasingly universal screening for Lynch syndrome by mismatch repair protein immunohistochemistry is recommended.

diagnosis: Lynch syndrome–associated upper tract urothelial carcinoma
legend: Mismatch repair immunostains were performed in this tumour for Lynch syndrome screening. Here, nuclear MLH1 expression is normal/retained, as expected for this case, in which MSH2 germline mutation was eventually proved by sequencing.

diagnosis: Lynch syndrome–associated upper tract urothelial carcinoma
legend: Mismatch repair immunostains were performed in this tumour for Lynch syndrome screening. Here, nuclear MSH2 expression is absent/lost in tumour cells but retained in inflammatory cells (internal control). This abnormal pattern was expected for this case, in which MSH2 germline mutation was eventually proved by sequencing.

diagnosis: Lynch syndrome–associated upper tract urothelial carcinoma
legend: Mismatch repair immunostains were performed in this tumour for Lynch syndrome screening. Here, nuclear MSH6 expression is absent/lost in tumour cells but retained in inflammatory cells (internal control). This abnormal pattern was expected in this case, in which MSH2 germline mutation was eventually proved by sequencing. If MSH2 is mutated, MSH6 expression is often lost as well, because of its dimerization with MSH2.

diagnosis: Lynch syndrome–associated upper tract urothelial carcinoma
legend: Mismatch repair immunostains were performed in this tumour for Lynch syndrome screening. Here, nuclear PMS2 expression is present in tumour cells, as expected for this case, in which MSH2 germline mutation was eventually proved by sequencing.

diagnosis: Lynch syndrome–associated upper tract urothelial carcinoma
legend: These tumours often show at least a focal inverted growth pattern, and overall they lack pleomorphism and subtype differentiation. A pushing, non-infiltrative stromal interface is often apparent, although such features are insufficient to facilitate prospective recognition.
